$comment: Neutral shipped <sys/ioctl.h> (POSIX) — c16 (SQLite os_unix) + TF-C92 (the request-ENCODING macros). SQLite calls ioctl in a few places (e.g. F2FS / proxy-locking paths). Verified against glibc misc/sys/ioctl.h + xnu/bsd/sys/ioctl.h: the prototype `int ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, ...)` is IDENTICAL on glibc and Darwin — variadic, the request arg is `unsigned long` (u64 on LP64) on both → a flat variadic signature `fn(i32, u64, ...) -> i32` (the c14c variadic-extern path). Gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho]. | ★ TF-C92 CORRECTION — the pre-c92 comment here asserted 'the _IOC/_IOR/_IOW request-ENCODING macros differ per-OS, but SQLite doesn't use this header's macros, so none are shipped (no over-ship)'. The second clause was FALSE and it cost a whole TU. SQLite uses them at TWO MEASURED sites: (1) macho — sqlite/src/os_unix.c:2986 `#define afpfsByteRangeLock2FSCTL _IOWR('z', 23, struct ByteRangeLockPB2)`, live under the os_unix.c:2966 guard `#if defined(__APPLE__) && SQLITE_ENABLE_LOCKING_STYLE` (`__APPLE__` is a macho-gated DSS predefine and LOCKING_STYLE self-defaults to 1 on Apple at os_unix.c:66-70), the tag declared at os_unix.c:2976 and the macro consumed at os_unix.c:3013 `err = fsctl(path, afpfsByteRangeLock2FSCTL, &pb, 0);`; (2) elf — os_unix.c:392-396, `_IO(F2FS_IOCTL_MAGIC, 1|2|3|5)` ×4 plus `_IOR(F2FS_IOCTL_MAGIC, 12, u32)` under `#ifdef __linux__`. An angle `#include` resolves to DESCRIPTORS ONLY (the real <sys/ioccom.h> / <asm-generic/ioctl.h> TEXT is never read), so with no descriptor row `_IOWR` survived to the parser as a CALL whose 3rd argument is a type-name — `struct` cannot start an expression → `error[P0009] … got 'struct'` at os_unix.c:2986:56, MEASURED as the sole diagnostic in that TU (a parse death, hence a FLOOR: it aborts before semantic analysis). | ENCODINGS, both MEASURED from a real header ON DISK, then differentially re-verified by compiling each replacement string beside the genuine macro. macho ← /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/sys/ioccom.h: IOCPARM_MASK 0x1fff, IOC_VOID 0x20000000, IOC_OUT 0x40000000, IOC_IN 0x80000000, IOC_INOUT (IN|OUT) 0xc0000000, `_IOC(inout,group,num,len) (inout | ((len & IOCPARM_MASK) << 16) | ((group) << 8) | (num))`. elf ← musl arch/generic/bits/ioctl.h (the Linux asm-generic ABI, verbatim on this machine under the emsdk sysroot): `_IOC(a,b,c,d) (((a)<<30) | ((b)<<8) | (c) | ((d)<<16))` with _IOC_NONE 0U / _IOC_WRITE 1U / _IOC_READ 2U, i.e. DIR at bit 30 (2-bit field), SIZE at 16, TYPE at 8, NR at 0 — so _IOWR's dir is 3u (READ|WRITE), NOT a single bit as on Darwin. The two OSes disagree on the DIRECTION FIELD ENTIRELY (Darwin: one bit each at 29/30/31, VOID has its own bit; Linux: a 2-bit code at 30, NONE=0) — this is exactly the per-OS divergence that belongs in `when:{format}` rows and NOWHERE else. Cross-checks: macho `_IOWR('z',23,struct ByteRangeLockPB2)` = 0xc0207a17 (sizeof 32 → 0x20<<16, 'z'=0x7a<<8, 23) — byte-identical to the SDK macro; elf `_IOR(0xf5,12,u32)` = 0x8004f50c and `_IO(0xf5,1..5)` = 0xf501/f502/f503/f505 — the published Linux F2FS_IOC_* numbers, which is an INDEPENDENT witness that the musl formula was transcribed correctly. | ★ THE DIRECTION BITS ARE UNSIGNED (`0x…u` / `0u`/`1u`/`2u`/`3u`) — interop-critical, and MEASURED rather than assumed, because the two halves of that claim are not equally true. Darwin spells them `(__uint32_t)0x…` and musl spells them `0U/1U/2U` for one reason: the result widens to the `unsigned long` request parameter of ioctl/fsctl, and a SIGNED top-bit value that sign-extends passes a WRONG REQUEST NUMBER — a silent wrong-value miscompile at the syscall boundary, never a diagnostic. On the MACHO arms the `u` is EXPLICITNESS, not a repair: `0xc0000000` already has type `unsigned int` by C 6.4.4.1p5 (it does not fit in `int`), and DSS + clang were measured to agree on `(unsigned long)0xc0000000 == 0xc0000000`. On the ELF arms it is genuinely LOAD-BEARING: `2 << 30` OVERFLOWS a signed int, and the two compilers DIVERGE on that UB — clang widens the fold to 0xffffffff80000000, DSS widens it to 0x80000000 — so a signed spelling would make DSS compute an ioctl number that disagrees with every native consumer of the same header, while `2u << 30` makes them agree. Hence the suffix on EVERY arm: it removes the question instead of resting on a per-compiler UB choice or on the escalation rule happening to rescue the Darwin case. `examples/c/shipped_ioctl_iowr_macho/` pins the exact encoded values with `_Static_assert` (plus a forward guard that the widening never sign-extends), so a shift/mask/direction regression is RED at compile time rather than a bad ioctl at runtime; MEASURED reds: deleting the `_IOWR` row restores P0009 at os_unix.c:2986:56, deleting only its macho VARIANT does the same (so variant SELECTION is pinned too), and giving macho `_IOR` the elf direction code fails the value assert loud. | FAMILY COMPLETENESS — a real tension, recorded not resolved-in-silence. TF-C90's lesson says descriptor COMPLETENESS is a correctness requirement, because a winning descriptor SHADOWS the real header that would have carried the missing names; here the shadowing is TOTAL (the header text is never read), so this descriptor is the ONLY source of these names, and a `#if defined(_IOW)` probe turns an under-shipped family into a SILENTLY-WRONG BRANCH rather than a loud absence. The no-over-ship rule pulls the other way: every unexercised row is a claim no test checks, and an untested claim is how the false comment above survived. RESOLUTION: ship the CLOSED, PORTABLE set of four — `_IO`/`_IOR`/`_IOW`/`_IOWR` — identical in name, arity and meaning on both shipped OSes, every one MEASURED from a real header and every one value-pinned by tests/ffi + the corpus example (so completeness costs no unverified surface). `_IOW` and macho `_IOR`/`_IO` exceed the corpus's current demand DELIBERATELY: they are the same one formula the corpus rows already prove, differing only in the direction constant. DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: `_IOC` and the direction-bit vocabulary (`IOC_VOID`/`IOC_OUT`/`IOC_IN`/`IOC_INOUT`/`IOCPARM_MASK` on Darwin, `_IOC_NONE`/`_IOC_WRITE`/`_IOC_READ` on Linux). Those are the IMPLEMENTATION vocabulary, not a portable interface — the two OSes disagree on both the spellings and the bit layout, so `_IOC` is unusable without also shipping per-OS names that no corpus site references (verified: zero hits for IOC_*/IOCPARM_*/_IOC_* across sqlite src/ + ext/) and whose mere availability would invite a portability bug. Their absence is LOUD, not silent: `_IOC(...)`/`IOC_OUT` reach the parser as an undeclared function/identifier → S0001. Each of the four rows therefore INLINES its numerics and is self-contained — no `constants` surface, and no macro body that depends on another descriptor macro expanding inside it. | ★ THE ONE HAZARD THE ENUMERATION ABOVE OMITS — the SIZE FIELD is UNBOUNDED in both arms, and each one overflows DIFFERENTLY and SILENTLY. macho MASKS (`sizeof(t) & 0x1fffu`, verbatim from the SDK's IOCPARM_MASK 0x1fff at sys/ioccom.h:74), so a type LARGER than 8191 bytes is truncated to its low 13 bits — a 8192-byte type encodes size 0, giving an ioctl number that is well-formed, wrong, and diagnostic-free. elf does NOT mask (`sizeof(t) << 16`, verbatim from the musl `_IOC`), so the field just keeps growing: at `sizeof(t) >= 0x4000` bit 30 lights up and the value collides with the 2-bit DIRECTION field — a 0x4000-byte `_IOR` encodes as 0x80000000|0x40000000, which IS `_IOWR`, so the kernel would copy the argument the WRONG WAY. Both arms faithfully reproduce their source header, and that is the point: NEITHER USERSPACE HEADER GUARDS THIS EITHER. MEASURED on this machine — `grep -r _IOC_TYPECHECK` over the emsdk musl sysroot returns ZERO hits, and Darwin sys/ioccom.h carries no compile-time check. The guard that exists is KERNEL-INTERNAL: Linux include/uapi/asm-generic/ioctl.h defines `_IOC_TYPECHECK(t)` as `(sizeof(t) == sizeof(t[1]) && sizeof(t) < (1 << _IOC_SIZEBITS)) ? sizeof(t) : __invalid_size_argument_for_IOC` — a deliberate compile/link error — only under `#ifdef __KERNEL__`, while the userspace `#else` arm is a bare `sizeof(t)`. So DSS is EXACTLY as unguarded as a real userspace program, which makes this a recorded LIMIT rather than a divergence from the source header. NOT TRIGGERED TODAY: every corpus use is small — `struct ByteRangeLockPB2` 32 bytes, `u32` 4, `_IO` 0 — so no shipped site is near either wall and a value pin here would be a claim about types nobody passes. Closing it means a size ceiling INSIDE the macro expansion (a `_Static_assert`-bearing replacement, or a descriptor-level typecheck facet), which is a mechanism and not a row — and the ceiling is PER-FORMAT (8191 macho vs 16383 elf), so it belongs in these same `when:{format}` arms. | ARCH CAVEAT (elf): the asm-generic direction layout is Linux's DEFAULT, and a few architectures override it (ppc/alpha/mips/sparc use NONE=1/READ=2/WRITE=4 with a different size field). DSS's elf targets are x86_64 + arm64, both asm-generic, so `when:{format:elf}` is exact for every target that ships today. It is NOT extensible to such an arch: a macro variant's `when` is FORMAT-ONLY by construction (src/ffi/shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp — arch is not threaded into the preprocessor), so an elf/ppc64 target would need that selector widened rather than another row here.
